title: Enemy Names over Enemies in Rm2k3

posts.author: ZENWARECO
posts.body:
Yet I still do.  The people today want the newer ones!
Anyway, in 2003, how would I make enemy names appear over an enemy when the 'cursor' is ON the enemy.
Best bet, is in Paint or Photoshop, logically. That's a lot of work though.  Is there a work around? With or without Goliath or David? :/
I'm not really sure myself.
Thanks all, if anyone can help.

posts.author: DevRPG2k
posts.body:
If you were trying to change the layout of the entire battle system, I would recommend creating your own system with events, but recreating the existing system with one or two small changes would be frustrating and probably wouldn't even give you a 100% working system.
Just change the interface in the database to
Type A

posts.body:
I kind of recall that someone out there, made it possible to do with states and conditions. Though you would have to do it with adding conditions on enemies on the zeroth page.
That first system feels too FF ish. :/

posts.author: DevRPG2k
posts.body: It is impossible to read the game database to get the names of the monsters only by events, and if it is a "PSEUDO" method there is still no conditional or possibility to identify when the cursor (Hand) is selecting a target (enemy), if this happened in some project it was due to some modification or more likely a battle system made entirely by events

posts.author: ZENWARECO
posts.body:
Er sorry wrong wording.
I saw it in a game. It was done with states, not conditional branch. My bad.
Though it looked like there were states, with shortened monster names. Not full. Bc in a state, all you can fit is 8 characters. I think.
Then, in a battle event page, on the zeroth page, states are added, according to how many monsters there are. If 4, then 4 states on each monster. And this is before the battle starts.
And when you hover over the monster, voila, the state message shows up.
I think this was in Phantasia 3. I think...
Worked that way. Ill see if i can find an example.
